english.q: What is the largest planet in our solar system?
english.text:
The largest planet in our solar system is **Jupiter**.

It is a gas giant with a mass more than twice that of all the other planets in the solar system combined. Jupiter's equatorial diameter is approximately **139,820 kilometers** (83,769 miles), which is about 11 times wider than Earth. Due to its immense size and low density, it could theoretically fit more than 1,300 Earths inside it.

english.q: What is the boiling point of water in Celsius?
english.text:
The boiling point of water at standard atmospheric pressure (1 atmosphere or 101.325 kPa) is **100°C**.

This is the temperature at which liquid water turns into vapor and is widely used as the upper fixed point for the Celsius temperature scale. Note that this temperature can change slightly depending on the altitude and atmospheric pressure; for example, water boils at a lower temperature at high altitudes.

english.q: How many minutes are in an hour?
english.text:
There are **60** minutes in an hour.

This is the standard definition used in the Gregorian calendar and most other timekeeping systems globally. An hour is simply defined as 60 minutes, which is why you don't have to do any math if you are just trying to figure out how long something takes.

english.q: Which ocean is the largest?
english.text:
The largest ocean in the world is the **Pacific Ocean**.

It covers an area of approximately **165.25 million square kilometers** (63.8 million square miles), which is more than twice the size of the next largest ocean, the Atlantic Ocean. The Pacific Ocean is so large that it contains more than 30% of the Earth's surface and holds about 44% of the world's total ocean volume. It is also the deepest ocean, with the Challenger Deep reaching a depth of over 10,900 meters.

english.q: What is the capital of Italy?
english.text:
The capital of Italy is **Rome** (Italian: *Roma*).

Located in the central part of the Italian Peninsula, Rome is not only the political and administrative center of the country but also its largest city and the capital of the Lazio region. It is renowned for its rich history, as it was the capital of the Roman Empire, and is home to numerous historic landmarks such as the Colosseum, the Vatican City, and the Pantheon.
